chunks: Hadith 5115 — Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who stole, so his right hand was cut off; then he stole again, so his left foot was cut off; then he stole a third time, he said:

“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام would confine him permanently in prison and would say: ‘Indeed I am ashamed before my Lord to leave him without a hand with which he cleans himself and without a foot with which he walks to his need.’”
He said: “And when he cut the hand, he cut it below the joint; and when he cut the foot, he cut it from the ankle.”
He said: “And he did not hold that anything from the hudud should be remitted.”

key_terms.السِّجْنِ: prison; the punishment mentioned for the third theft
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal punishments; punishments not to be remitted
key_terms.الْكَعْبِ: the ankle; the point from which the foot was cut
key_terms.الْمَفْصِلِ: the joint; the point below which the hand was cut
key_terms.الْيُسْرَى: the left side; here, the left foot
key_terms.الْيُمْنَى: the right side; here, the right hand
key_terms.سَرَقَ: stole; the act that triggers the legal punishment discussed here
key_terms.فَقُطِعَتْ: was cut off; referring to the implementation of the hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a thief who steals a third time after the hand and foot have already been cut?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the ruling concerning repeated theft after the prescribed amputations have already been carried out. It presents the practice of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in imprisoning the offender thereafter, while also specifying the places of amputation and affirming that the prescribed hudud were not to be waived.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5115 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) regarding a man who stole, and his right hand was cut off. Then he stole again, and his left foot was cut off. Then he stole a third time.
Imam (as) said: "Commander of the Faithful (as) would imprison him for life and would say, 'I feel ashamed before my Lord (azj) to leave him without a hand to clean himself with and without a foot to walk with to fulfill his needs.'"
Imam Al-Baqir (as) added: "When Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) would cut off the hand, he would cut it below the wrist joint, and when he would cut off the foot, he would cut it from the ankle."
Imam Al-Baqir (as) also stated: "Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) did not believe that any of the prescribed punishments should be pardoned."
